Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · School & learning

editor noun

of a newspaper, magazine or book

also editors, editor in chief, chief editor, newspaper editor

modern

Traupman 308: redāctor prīnceps, editor in chief
Traupman 308

1redāctor: long a. From redāctus, redigō (agō, āctus): Lachmann’s law. Traupman 308 prints redāctor. Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.

redāctor1, redāctōris m.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

editor (of a newspaper, magazine, book); a woman is redāctrīx

A modern coinage from redigō, to bring into order. The long ā by Lachmann’s law, as in āctus.

Other words

  • ēmendātor, ēmendātōris m. — a corrector; one who edits a text

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Balb. 20: corrector atque ēmendātor nostrae cīvitātis (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. edit (ēmendāre) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically anyone who corrects or improves something, a state as much as a text; fits the editor who prepares or corrects a text (ēmendāre, Morgan–Owens), not the editor who runs a paper.

  • ēditor, ēditōris m. — editor (of a newspaper or magazine)

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · Traupman 308 (printed editor, without the macron) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Modern, after ēdere, to publish (librum ēdere, Cic.). Classically the word means only “that which brings forth” (Lucan 2.423) and, late, a giver of games (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Hanc commentātiōnem redāctōrī mitte.

    Send this article to the editor.composed

See also newspaper, journalist, article, magazine.

SourcesLewis & Short: emendator · Lewis & Short: editor · Lewis & Short: redigo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 308, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026). Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. edit (prepare a text for publication).

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
